extracted_claims.text: Under the original AI Act text (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III were to become subject to obligations 36 months after entry into force, i.e. 2 August 2026.

The AI Omnibus / Digital Omnibus on AI Regulation (amending Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, referred to as Regulation (EU) 2026/1744) extended the application date for Annex III high-risk AI obligations from 2 August 2026 to 2 December 2027.

The political agreement on the AI Omnibus amendments was reached on 7 May 2026, the Omnibus was adopted on 19 November 2025 as a legislative proposal, and the final amending Regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026.

The consolidated EUR-Lex text (version dated 27.07.2026) and the AI Act Service Desk's Article 111 commentary reference 'the date of application of Chapter III' / 2 August 2026 in connection with operators of high-risk systems placed on the market before that date, reflecting pre-amendment wording in some places.
Separately, obligations for high-risk AI systems that are safety components of products regulated under EU product-safety harmonisation legislation (Annex I) apply from 2 August 2028.

Transparency obligations under Article 50 generally apply from 2 August 2026, with a transition until 2 December 2026 for marking/detection obligations under Article 50(2) for systems already on the market.
New prohibitions on non-consensual sexual deepfakes and CSAM-generating systems, and the Article 50(2) transition deadline, start to apply 2 December 2026.

The Commission had proposed adjusting the timeline for high-risk AI rules by up to 16 months so that rules would start applying once the Commission confirms needed standards and tools are available, rather than on a fixed date.

As of April 2026, absent enactment of the Omnibus amendments, the applicable date in law for Annex III obligations remained 2 August 2026, creating timeline pressure to pass the amendments before that date.
Per Article 113 as amended, Chapter III Sections 1–3 (covering Annex III high-risk systems), with the exception of Article 6(5), apply from 2 December 2027.

A news/blog source asserts, without citation to any legal text, that every high-risk AI system needs an 'algorithm passport' registered with the AI Office before first use, framed as a legal requirement.

report:
# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The original text of the EU AI Act set 2 August 2026 as the date Annex III high-risk AI system obligations would take effect, but this has since been superseded: the AI Omnibus amendment, which entered into force on 27 July 2026, extended the application date to **2 December 2027** (high confidence). Some legal databases and commentary have not fully caught up with this change, creating confusion between the original and amended deadlines.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline
Under the original Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III were due to apply 36 months after entry into force, corresponding to 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [Squire Patton Boggs](https://www.squirepattonboggs.com/media/h3pcmbj2/ai-timeline-implementation-and-compliance.pdf)).

### The Omnibus Amendment
The AI Omnibus / Digital Omnibus on AI Regulation amended Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 and extended the Annex III application date from 2 August 2026 to **2 December 2027** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). Some sources identify this amending act as Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (high confidence per corroboration across multiple sources), though it should be noted that the official EU guidance sources (e.g., the AI Act Service Desk and Digital Strategy pages) do not themselves cite this specific number, while several commentary sources do ([Questa AI](https://www.questa-ai.com/privacy-cafe/eu-ai-act-countdown-is-your-annex-iii-system-ready-for-august-2026), [annexops.com](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027), [euaicompass.com](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)) — this specific numbering is treated as corroborated but worth independent legal verification given the gap in official sourcing. Political agreement on these amendments was reached on 7 May 2026, with adoption as a legislative proposal on 19 November 2025 and entry into force of the final amending Regulation on 27 July 2026 (high confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules), [Shaping Europe's Digital Future](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)). The Commission had proposed adjusting the timeline by up to 16 months so that rules would apply once the Commission confirms the necessary standards and tools are available, rather than on a fixed calendar date (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)) — it is unclear whether this conditional mechanism, or a fixed backstop date, was ultimately adopted.

### Related Deadlines
High-risk AI systems that are safety components of products under existing EU product-safety legislation (Annex I) remain subject to a separate, later deadline of 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [euaicompass.com](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)). Separately, transparency obligations under Article 50 generally still apply from 2 August 2026, with a further transition to 2 December 2026 for marking/detection duties under Article 50(2) for systems already on the market (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk timeline](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)). Separately and with lower certainty, new prohibitions on non-consensual sexual deepfakes and CSAM-generating systems are also reported to start applying 2 December 2026 (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk timeline](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
There is a clear contradiction between sources: pre-Omnibus and non-updated commentary continues to cite 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline ([Cloud Security Alliance](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20), [Responsible AI Labs, published April 2026](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance)), while post-Omnibus official EU guidance confirms the date moved to 2 December 2027 ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)). The later-in-time amending Regulation controls. Notably, the EUR-Lex consolidated text and the Article 111 guidance still reference "the date of application of Chapter III" / 2 August 2026 in places, suggesting incomplete consolidation of the amendment (high confidence claim, but internally inconsistent) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [Article 111 commentary](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)). A claim that pre-Omnibus law required 2 August 2026 "absent enactment" of the amendments, as of April 2026, is flagged as **low confidence (0.17)** ([LinkedIn/Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)). A specific claim citing Article 113 for the 2 December 2027 date, excepting Article 6(5), is also **low confidence (0.12)** ([ai-act-law.eu](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). An unsupported claim about an "algorithm passport" registration requirement is **low confidence (0.12)** and uncorroborated by any official source ([ai-compliance-hub.example](https://ai-compliance-hub.example/high-risk-ai-checklist)).

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear whether official texts (EUR-Lex, Article 111 guidance) have been fully updated to reflect 2 December 2027. The exact legal citation number for the amending act (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, per commentary sources) is not independently confirmed by any official EU source reviewed here. Whether the Commission's proposed conditional 16-month delay (tied to standards readiness) was adopted verbatim, and how the 2 December 2027 date interacts with the Article 6(5)/6(1) exceptions, are unresolved.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The original text of the EU AI Act set 2 August 2026 as the date Annex III high-risk AI system obligations would take effect, but this has since been superseded: the AI Omnibus amendment, which entered into force on 27 July 2026, extended the application date to **2 December 2027** (high confidence). Some legal databases and commentary have not fully caught up with this change, creating confusion between the original and amended deadlines.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline
Under the original Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III were due to apply 36 months after entry into force, corresponding to 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [Squire Patton Boggs](https://www.squirepattonboggs.com/media/h3pcmbj2/ai-timeline-implementation-and-compliance.pdf)).

### The Omnibus Amendment
The AI Omnibus / Digital Omnibus on AI Regulation amended Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 and extended the Annex III application date from 2 August 2026 to **2 December 2027** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). Political agreement on these amendments was reached on 7 May 2026, with adoption as a legislative proposal on 19 November 2025 and entry into force of the final amending Regulation on 27 July 2026 (high confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules), [Shaping Europe's Digital Future](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)). The Commission had proposed adjusting the timeline by up to 16 months so that rules would apply once the Commission confirms the necessary standards and tools are available, rather than on a fixed calendar date (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)) — it is unclear whether this conditional mechanism, or a fixed backstop date, was ultimately adopted.

### Related Deadlines
High-risk AI systems that are safety components of products under existing EU product-safety legislation (Annex I) remain subject to a separate, later deadline of 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [euaicompass.com](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)). Transparency obligations under Article 50 generally still apply from 2 August 2026, with a further transition to 2 December 2026 for marking/detection duties under Article 50(2) (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk timeline](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)). New prohibitions on non-consensual sexual deepfakes and CSAM-generating systems also start applying 2 December 2026 (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk timeline](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
There is a clear contradiction between sources: pre-Omnibus and non-updated commentary continues to cite 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline ([Cloud Security Alliance](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20), [Responsible AI Labs, published April 2026](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance)), while post-Omnibus official EU guidance confirms the date moved to 2 December 2027 ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)). The later-in-time amending Regulation controls. Notably, the EUR-Lex consolidated text and the Article 111 guidance still reference "the date of application of Chapter III" / 2 August 2026 in places, suggesting incomplete consolidation of the amendment (high confidence claim, but internally inconsistent) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [Article 111 commentary](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)). A claim that pre-Omnibus law required 2 August 2026 "absent enactment" of the amendments is flagged as low confidence (0.17) ([LinkedIn/Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)). A specific claim citing Article 113 for the 2 December 2027 date, excepting Article 6(5), is also low confidence (0.12) ([ai-act-law.eu](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). An unsupported claim about an "algorithm passport" registration requirement is low confidence (0.12) and uncorroborated by any official source ([ai-compliance-hub.example](https://ai-compliance-hub.example/high-risk-ai-checklist)).

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear whether official texts (EUR-Lex, Article 111 guidance) have been fully updated to reflect 2 December 2027. The precise legal citation number for the amending act (possibly Regulation (EU) 2026/1744) is not confirmed by official sources. Whether the Commission's proposed conditional 16-month delay (tied to standards readiness) was adopted verbatim, and how the 2 December 2027 date interacts with the Article 6(5)/6(1) exceptions, are unresolved.
